login.headline: Command every stage of your cloud.
login.intro: OrkStage turns templates into running customer environments on any cloud, and plans every change before it happens.

points.provisionTitle: Provision on AWS, Azure and OCI from one control plane
points.provisionDetail: Place each part of an environment in the account and region where it belongs.
points.planTitle: Every change is planned, checked against policy and audited
points.planDetail: Review the plan and the estimated cost before anything touches your cloud.
points.healthTitle: Health, incidents and status pages built in
points.healthDetail: Watch every stage and keep customers informed without extra tools.

login.footer: Multicloud control plane for platform, SRE and DevOps teams.
login.title: Sign in
login.subtitle: Use your organization's single sign on.
login.providersUnavailable: Sign in providers are unavailable right now.
login.noProviders: No single sign on provider is configured.

notifications.title: Notifications

onboarding.title: Set the stage
onboarding.intro: Five steps from an empty console to a running, monitored environment. {done} of {total} done.

steps.targetLabel: Connect or validate a cloud target
steps.targetHint: Give OrkStage an account to build on, or a mock target to rehearse.
steps.templateHint: Start from a system template or build your own in the visual builder.

steps.planHint: See every change and the approximate monthly cost before anything runs.
steps.deployHint: Follow the rollout live, then keep watch from the status page.

plan.policyFailures: {count, plural, one {# policy failure} other {# policy failures}}
plan.validationHint: Schema, semantic and capability checks, with suggested fixes.
plan.connectivityHint: How resources reach each other. Links between clouds are highlighted.
plan.estimatedCostHint: Monthly estimate. Approximate, not an invoice.

deployments.emptyBody: Deploy an instance and its rollout shows up here, step by step.
deployments.title: Deployments
deployments.description: Every rollout and teardown across your fleet, newest first. Open one to follow it step by step.

detail.simulatedBody: This deployment runs against the mock provider. No real cloud resources are created or changed.
detail.awaiting: This deployment is waiting for approval.
detail.awaitingRisk: This deployment is waiting for approval (plan risk: {risk}).
detail.reviewPlanApprove: Review the plan below and approve to continue.
detail.noSteps: Steps show up once the worker picks up the deployment.
detail.cancelBody: Cancellation is cooperative: the step in progress finishes, then the remaining steps are skipped. Resources already created are kept. A destroy removes them, or a later deploy reconciles them.
detail.outputsHint: Secrets are shown only as references.

overview.noTenantBody: Ask your organization admin to add you to a tenant.
overview.title: Overview
overview.description: Your fleet at a glance: health, deployments and spend across every cloud.
overview.noTargetsBody: Connect a cloud account, or register a mock target, before your first deploy.
overview.attentionHint: What needs an operator right now.

trends.heading: Last {days} days

instances.title: Instances
instances.description: Each instance is a customer environment with its services, data and networking, wherever they run.
instances.emptyFilteredBody: Clear a filter to see more of the fleet.
instances.emptyBody: Create an instance from a template to put your first environment on stage.

wizard.title: New instance
wizard.description: Create an environment from a template. Nothing is created in the cloud until you review the plan and deploy.
wizard.createFailed: The instance could not be created

tenant.title: Choose the customer
tenant.hint: The instance and its cost belong to this tenant.

template.noneBody: Publish a template version before creating instances.
template.title: Choose a template
template.hint: A template describes services, data and networking. Only published versions can be used.
template.planMismatch: Not listed for the {plan} plan. The API may reject it.
template.notForProductionBody: This template trades resilience for cost (single zone, minimal sizes, no high availability, short retention). Use it only for validation and sandboxes.

placement.title: Choose where each part runs
placement.hint: Each placement slot is bound to a cloud target (account) and a region. Slots can use different clouds.
placement.useSame: Use the same target for all slots
placement.useSameHint: Copies the "{slot}" binding to every compatible slot (deploy on a single cloud).
placement.skipped: The target does not support these slots: {slots}. Pick a target for them manually.
placement.noTarget: No active cloud target supports this slot.

variables.title: Variables
variables.none: This template has no variables. The template author fixed its sizing.
variables.configureHint: Defaults are prefilled. The API validates the values again.

details.title: Name and environment
details.name: Display name
details.slugHint: Used in resource names and URLs. You type it again to confirm a destroy.
details.nonProductionWarning: The selected template is marked as not for production. Consider a sandbox or development environment.

review.title: Review
review.hint: Creating the instance saves its definition. Next you preview the plan and the estimated cost, then deploy.
review.name: Name

instance.deployBusy: A deployment is already in progress
instance.upgraded: Template version changed. Run a preview to review the changes, then deploy to apply them.
instance.upgradedTo: Template version changed to {version}. Run a preview to review the changes, then deploy to apply them.
instance.topologyHint: Grouped by provider, cloud target and region. Knowledge goes from DESIRED (planned) to KNOWN (recorded) to ACTUAL (observed).
instance.previewHint: The preview compiles the template, checks policies, estimates cost and computes the plan. Nothing changes.
instance.noPreviewBody: Run a preview to see validation issues, policy results, connectivity, cost and the change plan.

instanceDialogs.deployDescription: Applies the current template version and variables to the bound cloud targets.
instanceDialogs.deployBody: The deployment runs in the background and you can follow it live. High risk plans or protected environments may wait for approval.
instanceDialogs.simulatedNote: This instance uses mock targets: nothing is created in a real cloud.
instanceDialogs.destroyDescription: Deletes every cloud resource of this instance. You cannot undo this.
instanceDialogs.protected: This instance is protected from destroy. Remove the protection in its settings first.
instanceDialogs.destroyWarning: All {count, plural, one {# resource} other {# resources}} on every bound cloud target will be deleted, including databases and object storage. Backups follow the retention policy of each provider.
instanceDialogs.confirmMismatch: Type the instance slug exactly to confirm.
instanceDialogs.upgradeDescription: This changes only the definition. Preview the plan, then deploy to apply it.
instanceDialogs.noOtherVersion: No other published version of {name} is available. Current version: {version}.

telemetry.noResourcesLogs: No resources yet. Logs are available after a deploy.
telemetry.noResourcesMetrics: No resources yet. Metrics are available after a deploy.

topology.emptyBody: This instance has no resources yet. Run a preview to see what will be created, then deploy.
topology.diagramLabel: Topology diagram. Use the List view for a text alternative.
topology.runPreviewForLabels: Run a preview to label connections with their network strategy.

templates.title: Templates
templates.description: Build a template once and deploy it many times. Published versions never change, and each instance pins the version it runs.
templates.emptyBody: System templates ship with the platform. Create a template, or clone one to make it your own.
templates.readOnlyNoCreate: You do not have permission to create templates.
templates.readOnlySystem: System templates ship with the platform and are read only. Clone it to make your own version.
templates.readOnlyNoEdit: You can view this template but not change it.

newPage.title: New template
newPage.description: Paste YAML here, or start in the visual builder. It is saved as a draft that you publish once it validates.

detail.cloneDescription: Creates an organization template you can edit, starting from the latest version of this template.
detail.placementSlots: {count, plural, one {# placement slot} other {# placement slots}}
detail.published: Published. Instances can now use this version.
detail.sourceHint: YAML as submitted. Published versions cannot change.

editor.title: New version
editor.hint: Edit the YAML (increase metadata.version), validate, save as a draft, then publish.

cloneForm.name: Name
cloneForm.nameHint: Lowercase identifier, unique in your organization.

importPage.title: Import infrastructure
importPage.description: Bring existing Terraform, CloudFormation, Kubernetes or Compose setups into OrkStage. You get a draft template to review before anything is deployed.
importPage.uploadHint: Only IaC and manifest files are read (up to 5 MB). Your browser skips dependencies, build output and secret folders.
importPage.selected: {count, plural, one {# file selected} other {# files selected}}
importPage.selectedSkipped: {count, plural, one {# file selected} other {# files selected}}, {skipped} skipped.
importPage.pasteTitle: Paste a report from the CLI
importPage.pasteHint: Scan locally so your code never leaves your machine: run ork scan --format json and paste the output, or run ork import.
importPage.name: Template name
importPage.createAndOpen: Create draft and open the builder
importPage.askAdmin: A platform admin can turn this import into a template. Share the import id {id}.

builder.publishNeedsSave: Save a draft first. Publishing applies to the saved version.
builder.publishWhenReady: Publish it when you are ready. Published versions never change.
builder.published: Published. New instances can now use version {version}.
builder.paletteHint: Drag onto a lane, or use the add button.
builder.canvasLabel: Template canvas. Placement slots are lanes and resources are nodes. Drag between handles to connect them.

tips.lanes: Lanes are placement slots: each instance binds a slot to a cloud account and region.
tips.drag: Drag a resource into a lane to place it there.
tips.connect: Drag from the right handle of a node to another node to add a connection, dependency, ingress route or DNS target.
tips.keys: Delete removes the selection. Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y undo and redo.

builder.checkedLivePlan: Checked as you edit, for the {plan} plan.
builder.serverHint: Includes capability and policy checks the browser cannot run.
builder.cloneDescription: Creates an editable copy in your organization and opens it in the builder.
builder.nodeIssues: {errors, plural, one {# error} other {# errors}}, {warnings, plural, one {# warning} other {# warnings}}
builder.newSlotDescription: Everything runs in one account and region.

inspector.idTaken: Another resource already uses this id.
inspector.unknownType: Unknown resource type "{type}". Edit it in YAML.
inspector.idHint: Edges and variables refer to it. Renaming updates them.
inspector.placementHint: Or drag the node into another lane.
inspector.noRelationships: None. Drag from the right handle of a node to another node to connect them.
inspector.slotHint: Each instance binds every slot to a cloud target and region, so one template can span several clouds.
inspector.name: Name
inspector.allowedProvidersHint: None selected means any registered provider.
inspector.removeSlotBlocked: Move or remove its resources first. A template needs at least one slot.
inspector.modeHint: private-preferred falls back to TLS with an allowlist when a private link is not justified.
inspector.plansLabel: Plans this template is available on
inspector.variablesHint: Settings an operator can change per instance, each bound to one resource field.
inspector.yamlHint: The template document. Edits apply to the canvas as soon as they pass the schema.

kinds.routeHint: Traffic from the ingress goes to this service.
kinds.dnsHint: The DNS name points at this ingress.
kinds.connectivityHint: The source talks to the target over the network (protocol, port, privacy).
kinds.dependsOnHint: Create the target first. No network rule.

fields.jsonHint: JSON object. Provider specific escape hatch, less portable.

incidents.title: Incidents
incidents.description: Disruptions your customers see on their status pages. Health checks open incidents automatically, and you can declare one too.
incidents.emptyOpenBody: Health checks keep watch and open an incident automatically if something breaks.
incidents.emptyBody: Incidents show up here when declared or detected.
incidents.declareDescription: The incident is published on the status page of the tenant and notifies subscribers.

form.title: Title
form.messageHint: Shown publicly on the status page. Describe the impact, not internal details.

detail.timelineHint: Newest first. Updates are visible on the status page of the tenant.
detail.impactHint: Leave unchanged to keep the current impact.

cloudTargets.title: Cloud targets
cloudTargets.description: The cloud accounts your instances run on. Credentials stay in your secret store, and OrkStage keeps only references.
cloudTargets.emptyBody: Connect an AWS account, or register a mock target to simulate AWS, Azure or OCI without touching a real cloud.
cloudTargets.registerDescription: Only configuration that is not secret is stored. Secrets are passed as references that the worker resolves.
cloudTargets.validateDescription: Runs the provider adapter checks (identity, permissions, quotas) and stores the result.
cloudTargets.capabilitiesDescription: Service implementations this target can provide.
cloudTargets.simulatedCatalog: Simulated catalog of {provider}: the mock provider imitates these services without creating anything.

form.accountId: Enter the 12 digit AWS account id.
form.roleArn: Enter an IAM role ARN, for example arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/co-deploy
form.credentialRef: Use a reference such as env://NAME or aws-sm://name. Never paste the secret value itself.
form.defaultRegionInvalid: Must be one of the allowed regions.
form.secretKeys: Keys that look like secrets are not allowed in config: {keys}
form.name: Name
form.simulateHint: The cloud catalog the mock provider imitates. Nothing real is created.
form.externalIdHint: A reference such as env://ACME_AWS_EXTERNAL_ID or aws-sm://orkstage/acme-external-id, resolved when used. Never paste the secret value.
form.noAdapterFields: The console has no specific fields for {provider} yet. Provide its configuration (nothing secret) under Advanced settings.
form.scopeHint: Every tenant can use shared targets.
form.credentialHint: Optional, for example env://NAME or aws-sm://name.
form.extraHint: Only settings that are not secret. Keys that look like secrets are rejected.

applications.title: Applications
applications.description: The container images your instances run. Templates reference them as catalog://NAME, and every deploy pins an immutable digest.
applications.emptyBody: Applications show up here once images are registered for templates to use.

tenants.title: Tenants
tenants.description: The customers you run environments for: their plan and how many environments they have.
tenants.emptyBody: Add your first customer organization, then create instances for it.
tenants.dialogDescription: A tenant is an isolated customer organization with its own plan and instances.

form.name: Name
form.slugHint: Used in URLs and resource names. Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.
form.domainsHint: Separate with commas. Users who sign in with single sign on from these domains can join this tenant.

auditPage.title: Audit log
auditPage.description: Who did what, when, and whether it worked. Quote the correlation id when you contact support.
auditPage.emptyBody: Sign ins, deployments and configuration changes are recorded here.
auditPage.loaded: {count, plural, one {# event loaded} other {# events loaded}}

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.description: Connect pipelines, scripts and the ork CLI with API keys, and push events to your systems with signed webhooks.
integrations.needAdmin: You need to be an owner or admin of a tenant to manage its integrations.

keys.introTenant: Keys act inside {tenant} with the role you choose, and scopes narrow them further. Send them as Authorization: Bearer ork_KEY
keys.introOrg: Keys act across the organization with the role you choose, and scopes narrow them further. Send them as Authorization: Bearer ork_KEY
keys.emptyBody: Create one for a CI pipeline or for the ork CLI. The secret is shown only once.
keys.newDescription: Give it the least access the job needs. You can revoke it at any time.
keys.revokeDescription: Anything that uses this key stops working immediately. You cannot undo this.
keys.copyNow: Copy this key now. It is shown only once and cannot be recovered. If you lose it, create a new key.
keys.cliHint: For the CLI, run ork login --with-token and paste it, or set ORK_TOKEN in your pipeline secrets.
keys.name: Name
keys.nameHint: Where it is used, for example github-actions-deploy

webhooks.intro: Each delivery is signed: verify OrkStage-Signature with your secret and reject timestamps older than five minutes.
webhooks.emptyBody: Send deployment and incident events to Slack bridges, ticketing systems or your own services.
webhooks.failures: {count, plural, one {# failed attempt in a row} other {# failed attempts in a row}}
webhooks.deleteBody: Pending deliveries are dropped. You cannot undo this.
webhooks.newDescription: Endpoints must use https and a public address.
webhooks.secretDescription: Shown only once. Store it in the secret store of your receiver.
webhooks.descriptionHint: Optional, for example Ops alerts bridge
webhooks.noDeliveriesBody: Use Test to send a ping.
